content: To facilitate a smooth transition, the legislation provided a one-year grace period that officially concluded on June 30, 2021 [114] . For telecommunications companies, which act as custodians of vast repositories of sensitive consumer data, the implementation of POPIA necessitated a comprehensive overhaul of data management frameworks, privacy policies, and security infrastructures. The initial implementation period, spanning from 2020 to 2023, represented a critical phase during which telecom providers focused heavily on managed data handling, data protection, and privacy adherence. During this timeframe, organizations across South Africa encountered significant challenges in operationalizing compliance measures, particularly in navigating complex requirements such as ensuring lawful data processing, securing explicit consumer consent, establishing protocols for data breach notifications, and respecting the expanded rights of data subjects [113] . Following the expiration of the grace period, the Information Regulator, the body tasked with overseeing POPIA compliance, intensified its monitoring and enforcement efforts [111] . Although granular statistical data regarding specific penalties during the 2020 to 2023 period remains scarce, the broader consensus indicates that this era was pivotal for organizations striving to align their legacy systems with stringent new statutory requirements [114] . Telecommunications providers were compelled to embed fundamental privacy principles, such as data minimization and the rigorous safeguarding of information, into their core operational architectures. However, achieving full compliance proved to be an iterative and ongoing challenge. Reflections on this period suggest that many organizations required extended timelines and sought additional regulatory guidance to meet the evolving standards of data protection [115] . As of June 2026, the regulatory environment surrounding POPIA has seen significant advancements, characterized by stricter enforcement deadlines and a heightened emphasis on addressing firm-level compliance gaps . The persistence of compliance gap analyses as late as 2026 underscores the reality that organizations continue to face hurdles long after the initial grace period ended, highlighting the enduring and substantial influence of POPIA on data handling practices within the South African market [113] .
